rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains commanding one's family to pray as rescuing them from God's punishment through prayer, and says one must persevere in it.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها}

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Aslam recounts that ʿUmar kept a nightly prayer time and, when he awoke to pray, roused his household citing this command.
rows.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب كان يبيت عنده أنا ويرفأ، وكان له ساعة من الليل يصلي فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer brings provision from where one does not expect; he connects this promise to God's provision for the Godfearing and to humanity's purpose of worship.
rows.anchor: يعني (9) إذا أقمت الصلاة أتاك الرزق من حيث لا تحتسب

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawrī glosses the phrase to mean that God does not charge the Prophet with seeking provision.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري: {لا نسألك رزقا} أي: لا نكلفك الطلب.

rows.speaker: أبوه
rows.claim: Hishām's father would recite these verses after seeing worldly wealth, then urge his own household to pray.
rows.anchor: عن هشام، عن أبيه؛ أنه كان إذا دخل على أهل الدنيا، فرأى من دنياهم طرفا فإذا رجع إلى أهله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Thābit reports that when hardship struck the Prophet, he called his family to pray repeatedly.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصابه خصاصة نادى أهله: " يا أهلاه، صلوا، صلوا "

rows.speaker: ثابت
rows.claim: Thābit adds that prophets resorted to prayer whenever an urgent matter came upon them.
rows.anchor: قال ثابت: وكانت (1) الأنبياء إذا نزل بهم (2) أمر فزعوا إلى الصلاة. (3)

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In a divine report narrated by Abū Hurayra, God promises to fill with richness and relieve poverty whoever devotes themself to worship, while neglect leaves them busy and poor.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " يقول الله تعالى: يا ابن آدم تفرغ لعبادتي أملأ صدرك غنى، وأسد فقرك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet's teaching that making the Hereafter one's single concern suffices for worldly worries, while scattered worldly concerns leave one exposed to ruin.
rows.anchor: سمعت نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " من جعل الهموم هما واحدا هم المعاد كفاه الله هم دنياه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reports that worldly obsession brings disarray and poverty, whereas intending the Hereafter brings order, inward wealth, and worldly provision in spite of itself.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " من كانت الدنيا همه فرق الله عليه أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good end belongs to the Godfearing in this world and the next, culminating in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وحسن العاقبة في الدنيا والآخرة، وهي الجنة، لمن اتقى الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In an authentic report, the Prophet interprets dates from Ibn Ṭāb in a dream as foretelling the believers' good outcome in this world, elevation, and the soundness of their religion.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " رأيت الليلة كأنا في دار عقبة بن رافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns that the Hour is near while people remain heedless: they neither work for it nor prepare themselves.
rows.anchor: هذا تنبيه من الله، عز وجل، على اقتراب الساعة ودنوها، وأن الناس في غفلة عنها، أي: لا يعملون لها، ولا يستعدون من أجلها.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that the Prophet explained their heedlessness as being immersed in worldly life.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم {في غفلة معرضون} قال: "في الدنيا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the warning to God's command not to rush the coming judgment and to the report that the Hour has drawn near as the moon split, though disbelievers reject signs.
rows.anchor: اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر * وإن يروا آية يعرضوا ويقولوا سحر مستمر

rows.speaker: أبو العتاهية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAsākir records that Abū Nuwwās praised Abū al-ʿAtāhiya's couplet about people being heedless while death grinds on, as inspired by this verse.
rows.anchor: أشعر الناس الشيخ الطاهر أبو العتاهية حيث يقول: الناس في غفلاتهم … ورحا المنية تطحن

rows.speaker: عامر بن ربيعة
rows.claim: When an Arab offered him part of a valley granted by the Prophet, ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa declined, saying the newly revealed warning had made them forget worldly interests.
rows.anchor: فقال عامر: لا حاجة لي في قطيعتك، نزلت اليوم سورة أذهلتنا عن الدنيا

words: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is newly revealed; the Quraysh and other disbelievers hear each new revelation while playing and refusing to attend to it.
rows.anchor: محدث} أي: جديد إنزاله {إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

words: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address concerning those who ignore revelation is directed to Quraysh and disbelievers like them.
rows.anchor: والخطاب مع قريش ومن شابههم من الكفار

words: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِم
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asks why Muslims consult People of the Book about scriptures they altered, when their own Qur'an is the newest scripture and is read in an uncorrupted form; al-Bukhārī transmits a similar report.
rows.anchor: كما قال ابن عباس: ما لكم تسألون أهل الكتاب عما بأيديهم وقد حرفوه وبدلوه وزادوا فيه ونقصوا منه

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: The Arabs who asserted that angels were God's daughters are among those rebuked for claiming that God has offspring.
rows.anchor: كمن قال ذلك من العرب: إن الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting divine offspring, Ibn Kathīr explains that angels are honored servants of God, holding exalted ranks and obeying Him completely in word and deed.
rows.anchor: أي: الملائكة عباد الله مكرمون عنده، في منازل عالية ومقامات سامية، وهم له في غاية الطاعة قولا وفعلا

words: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels do not act or speak ahead of God, disobey His commands, or delay carrying them out; they hasten to obey.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يتقدمون بين يديه بأمر، ولا يخالفونه فيما أمر (1) به بل يبادرون إلى فعله

words: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge encompasses the angels, and nothing about them is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: وهو تعالى علمه محيط بهم، فلا يخفى عليه منهم خافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction of angelic intercession to those God approves is linked to the same rule in 2:255 and 34:23.
rows.anchor: ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Nawwās ibn Samʿān reports the Prophet's warning about the Dajjal: he is a curly-haired young man with a floating eye, emerges between Syria and Iraq, and believers must stand firm.
rows.anchor: ذكر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الدجال ذات غداة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the Dajjal remains forty days, the first like a year, the next like a month, the next like a week, and the rest ordinary; believers should estimate prayer times during the year-long day.
rows.anchor: قال: "أربعين يوما، يوم كسنة، ويوم كشهر، ويوم كجمعة، وسائر أيامه كأيامكم"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Dajjal travels as fast as wind-driven rain; those who accept him receive rain, crops, and thriving livestock, while those who reject him face famine and loss.
rows.anchor: فيمر بالحي فيدعوهم فيستجيبون له، فيأمر السماء فتمطر، والأرض فتنبت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: He commands a ruined place to yield its treasures, which follow him like swarms of bees; he then kills a man and the man returns to him radiant.
rows.anchor: ويمر بالخربة فيقول لها: أخرجي كنوزك، فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Jesus will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, pursue the Dajjal, and kill him at the eastern gate of Ludd.
rows.anchor: فبينما هم على ذلك، إذ بعث الله عز وجل المسيح ابن مريم، فينزل عند المنارة (2) البيضاء

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb reports that Gog and Magog repeatedly dig until they hear axes, but God restores the barrier each night; when one says they will emerge by God's will, they finally break through.
rows.anchor: قال كعب: إذا كان عند خروج يأجوج ومأجوج، حفروا حتى يسمع الذين يلونهم قرع فؤوسهم

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: The first waves drink a lake, the next lick its remaining mud, and the last find it dry; people flee, while the invaders' skyward arrows return bloodied and persuade them they have conquered heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: فتمر الزمرة الأولى بالبحيرة، فيشربون ماءها، ثم تمر الزمرة الثانية فيلحسون طينها

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Jesus prays for help; God sends worms to kill them and birds to carry their bodies to the sea, then a spring purifies the earth, which flourishes until one pomegranate feeds a household.
rows.anchor: فيقول: "اللهم، لا طاقة ولا يدين لنا بهم، فاكفناهم بما شئت"

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says that after news of Dhu al-Suwayqatayn, Jesus sends a vanguard of seven or eight hundred; a fragrant wind takes every believer, leaving people who mate like beasts as the Hour approaches.
rows.anchor: فبينما الناس كذلك إذ أتاهم الصريخ أن ذا السويقتين يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr regards this as one of Kaʿb al-Aḥbār's best accounts because authentic reports corroborate it.
rows.anchor: هذا من أحسن سياقات كعب الأحبار، لما شهد له من صحيح الأخبار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet saying that people will perform Hajj and ʿUmra at the Kaʿba after Gog and Magog emerge; al-Bukhārī alone transmits it.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ليحجن هذا البيت، وليعتمرن بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised truth is the Day of Resurrection; once its terrors, earthquakes, and upheavals occur, the Hour will be imminent.
rows.anchor: يعني: يوم القيامة، إذا وجدت هذه الأهوال والزلازل والبلابل، أزفت الساعة واقتربت

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the sight of these terrible events, disbelievers' eyes stare in shock and they cry woe, admitting they were heedless in worldly life and wronged themselves; the confession then cannot benefit them.
rows.anchor: أي: من شدة ما يشاهدونه من الأمور العظام: {يا ويلنا} أي: يقولون:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To answer deniers of resurrection, Ibn Kathīr points to God's power in the observable beginning of human creation: Adam was made from soil and his descendants from a lowly fluid.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى المخالف للبعث، المنكر للمعاد، ذكر تعالى الدليل على قدرته تعالى على المعاد، بما يشاهد من بدئه للخلق

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes development: after forty days sperm becomes a red clot for forty days, then an unformed flesh lump; it is shaped into the head, limbs, torso, and other organs, and miscarriages may occur before or after shaping.
rows.anchor: إذا استقرت النطفة في رحم المرأة، مكثت أربعين يوما كذلك، يضاف إليه ما يجتمع إليها، ثم تنقلب علقة حمراء بإذن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some pregnancies are not miscarried but remain in the womb until their appointed term, after which the child is brought forth.
rows.anchor: وتارة تستقر في الرحم لا تلقيها المرأة ولا تسقطها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the formed and unformed as a miscarried fetus, either formed or not formed.
rows.anchor: كما قال مجاهد في قوله تعالى: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: هو السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق.

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn, Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet saying that each person's creation passes through forty days as a drop, a clot, and a lump; an angel then writes the person's deeds, lifespan, provision, and fate before breathing in the spirit.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم -وهو الصادق المصدوق-:"إن خلق أحدكم يجمع في بطن أمه أربعين ليلة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reports an angel taking settled sperm and asking whether it is formed; if unformed it is miscarried as blood, while for the formed embryo its sex, fortune, lifespan, deeds, provision, and death-place are decreed.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم، أخذها (6) ملك بكفه

rows.speaker: عامر الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says that once the lump reaches its fourth formation it becomes a human being; if unformed, the womb expels it as blood.
rows.anchor: ثم تلا عامر الشعبي: {يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ḥudhayfa ibn Asīd, transmitted in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, says an angel enters the settled sperm after forty or forty-five days, records its sex, deeds, provision, lifespan, and destiny, and then closes the scroll so nothing changes.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة بن أسيد -يبلغ به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم-قال: "يدخل الملك على النطفة بعد ما تستقر في الرحم بأربعين أو خمس وأربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The newborn is weak in body, senses, strength, and reason; God gradually strengthens the child while parents care tenderly for them, until full strength and youthful beauty.
rows.anchor: أي: ضعيفا في بدنه، وسمعه وبصره وحواسه، وبطشه وعقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die in youth and full strength; others decline into senility, losing physical power, understanding, and memory, as also described in 30:54.
rows.anchor: أي: في حال شبابه وقواه

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas transmits a prophetic report: before puberty good deeds are credited to parents and sins are not charged; afterward deeds are recorded, with age-based blessings from forty through ninety, and at frailty past good works are still credited while sins are omitted.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك -رفع الحديث-قال: "المولود حتى يبلغ الحنث

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr calls the preceding age-blessings narration extremely unusual and severely objectionable, despite recording related versions.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث غريب جدا، وفيه نكارة شديدة

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A version suspended at Anas says a Muslim at forty is spared three afflictions; later ages bring easier reckoning, repentance, heavenly love, accepted good deeds, forgiveness, and intercession, with the person called God's prisoner on earth.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: إذا بلغ الرجل المسلم أربعين سنة، أمنه الله من أنواع البلايا، من الجنون والجذام والبرص

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A separate version raised to the Prophet through Ibn ʿUmar gives the same age-related blessings.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، مثله

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another report from Anas says that anyone who lives forty years in Islam is spared three kinds of affliction and then receives the age-based blessings described above.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من معمر يعمر في الإسلام أربعين سنة، إلا صرف الله عنه ثلاثة أنواع من البلاء

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Bazzār's version from Anas gives similar blessings by age: protection at forty, an easier account at fifty, repentance at sixty, forgiveness and heavenly love at seventy, acceptance at eighty, and forgiveness and intercession at ninety.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما من عبد يعمر في الإسلام أربعين سنة، إلا صرف الله عنه أنواعا من البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dormant earth is barren and without vegetation, providing another proof that God can revive the dead as He revives the earth.
rows.anchor: هذا دليل آخر على قدرته تعالى على إحياء الموتى، كما يحيي الأرض الميتة الهامدة، وهي القحلة التي لا نبت فيها ولا شيء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda describes the dormant earth as dusty and broken up.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: غبراء متهشمة. وقال السدي: ميتة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the dormant earth as dead.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: غبراء متهشمة. وقال السدي: ميتة

words: فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain makes the land move and revive; it rises as soil settles within it, then produces fruits and plants of varied colors, tastes, scents, shapes, and uses.
rows.anchor: أي: تحركت وحييت بعد موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A beautiful pair means plants that are pleasing to look at and pleasant in scent.
rows.anchor: أي: حسن المنظر طيب الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true Creator and governor who acts as He wills; reviving the earth shows that He revives the dead and has power over all things, as in 41:39 and 36:82.
rows.anchor: أي: الخالق المدبر الفعال لما يشاء
